newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN reports massacre of Hutu refugees in Burundi.
newsitem.headline: UN reports massacre of Hutu refugees in Burundi.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency UNHCR reported on Tuesday a new massacre of 60 people in violence-torn Burundi, most of them Hutu refugees who had returned home.

They were killed at a centre in the northwestern Cibitoke region on May 18, a spokeswoman said. Burundi's mainly Tutsi army, which grabbed power in a coup in 1996, has been forcibly relocating tens of thousands of members of the Hutu majority in such centres since last year.

It was the second massacre reported in the tiny central African country following the killing of 42 people, mostly Hutus, in a church at Rutenba hill in Muhuta commune, 27 km (17 miles) south of Bujumbura, on May 14.

UNHCR spokeswoman Pamela O'Toole did not say who was behind the latest killings. UNHCR appealed to regional countries not to force Burundian refugees home because of "unacceptable" levels of violence in the northwest, southwest and southeast, she said.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in massacres and in a civil war between Burundi's army and Hutu rebels since the first elected Hutu president was assassinated by troops in 1993.
UNHCR estimates that some 100,000 people have been displaced by the fighting in the Cibitoke province.
Tutsis are outnumbered four-to-one by Hutus in Burundi and many fear they will perish unless they block real power sharing.
